deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no derivation. It is a bibliographic list and continues the previous page, which headed 'Academische Schriften' and listed Euler's papers in the Petersburg Commentarii and the Paris Mémoires and prize volumes. Here the list goes on with Euler's papers in other journals:

(1) Miscellanea Berolinensia, Tom. VII (1743): 5 pieces.

(2) Mémoires de l'Académie royale des Sciences à Berlin, T. I–XXV: 120 pieces. Also two extracts of letters from Euler to (Johann III) Bernoulli and to Béguelin, in the Nouveaux Mémoires for 1772 and 1776. The 1772 letter is probably the one announcing that 2^31−1 is prime; the 1776 item is unsure.

(3) Acta Eruditorum Lipsiensia:
- 1733: 'Constructio aequationum quarundam differentialium quae indeterminatarum separationem non admittunt', on constructing differential equations whose variables cannot be separated.
- 1744: 'Solutio problematis ... mense [...] 1743 propositi'.
- 1773 (Nova Acta Eruditorum): 'Novae demonstrationes circa resolutionem numerorum in quadrata', i.e. Euler's work on representing numbers as sums of squares (E445).

(4) 'Journal litéraire de l'Allemagne', Jan.–Feb. 1751: 'Découverte d'une loi extraordinaire des nombres'. This is Euler's paper on the sum of divisors (E175). In it the divisor sum σ(n) obeys the pentagonal-number recurrence σ(n)=σ(n−1)+σ(n−2)−σ(n−5)−σ(n−7)+…, with the term σ(0) read as n.

(5) Miscellanea Taurinensia:
- Tome II (1760/61): letter to Lagrange on the propagation of disturbances in an elastic medium (E268).
- Tome III (1762–65): 'Éclaircissemens sur le mouvement des cordes vibrantes' (E317).
- Tome III: on the motion of strings of unequal thickness (E318).
- Tome III: on the integration of z_tt = a^2 z_xx + (b/x) z_x + (c/x^2) z (E319). The last term is cut off at the page edge; certainly the factor is z.
- Tome III: on new telescopes of five and six lenses and their further perfection.

The only mathematics written on the page is that partial differential equation. One known solvable case is the spherical wave equation, b=2a^2 and c=0, where z = F(x−at)/x + G(x+at)/x (my illustrative addition). The page is a reading or acquisition list of Euler's works, written on an interleaf bound into a printed German elementary mathematics textbook.
errors: The 1751 paper on the 'loi extraordinaire des nombres' (E175) appeared in the Bibliothèque impartiale (Jan.–Feb. 1751), not in a 'Journal littéraire de l'Allemagne'. The journal attribution on the page appears to be a slip, or a confusion with a different review journal.
The cord paper title is written 'inegalement epaisses'; Euler's actual title says 'inégalement grosses'. This is a paraphrase, not a mathematical error.
No mathematical derivations, so there are no computational errors to check.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely a bibliographic list of Euler's published papers, and Gauss's (or a contemporary's) close study of Euler is well known. It contains no original mathematics.

checkable.asserts: With b=2a^2 and c=0, z=F(x-at)/x solves Euler's equation; the expression should simplify to 0.
Euler's pentagonal recurrence for σ(12): σ(11)+σ(10)−σ(7)−σ(5)+σ(0), with σ(0) read as n=12, gives 28 = 12+18−8−6+12.
2^31−1 is prime (likely subject of the 1772 extract of Euler's letter to Bernoulli).

transcription_corrections: The final term of the equation, transcribed 'c/xx[?]', is cut off at the page edge. It is almost certainly '+ (c/xx) z' (Euler E319).
'aa(ddz/dx^2)' is correct; in the manuscript the first attempt at 'aa' is overwritten/smudged.
The right-hand page and the margin fragments belong to the printed facing textbook page, not to this manuscript leaf.
